articles.title: Andrew Milne, Kuunda co-founder, dies at 54
articles.summary:
Andrew Milne, the Kuunda co-founder who helped build the technology connecting banks to small businesses and mobile money users across Africa, died on October 13, the company said. He was 54.
Only days earlier, he celebrated completing a secondary share sale for the business he helped start in 2018. It was a moment to look ahead for Kuunda, as its early investors were seeing a return and the company was preparing for another phase of growth.
Now, his colleagues must carry those plans forward without him.
“Andy was an energetic and resilient leader,” Kuunda said in a statement. “He was much loved and deeply respected by everyone who worked alongside him.”
The company did not disclose the cause of death.
Milne founded Kuunda in 2018 with Sam Brawerman and Morné van der Westhuizen. Their starting point was a persistent cash flow problem that mobile money agents, small businesses, and consumers face despite being connected to digital payment networks. The team began designing its first liquidity product in Tanzania.
Kuunda built technology that allowed banks and digital platforms to offer credit within services people already used. The company used transaction data to help assess borrowers and embed overdrafts and working capital into services they already used.
It was work that could reach millions of people without making the company behind it a household name.

articles.title: Western open-weight models still can’t beat China
articles.summary:
A slew of new open-weight artificial intelligence models from American and European companies aim to convert users of Chinese open models who are concerned about security, but fall short of the dominant Chinese systems on performance despite having greater resources, experts said at a Rest of World event in San Francisco.
Last week, American startup Reflection launched its first open-weight model, and European labs Aleph Alpha and Mistral also released new open-weight models. Open models such as these offer users greater customization and control than the closed models of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google at significantly lower costs.
For businesses and governments in lower-income countries, in particular, cost is the primary factor, as well as the expertise needed to customize open models for their specific needs, including in areas such as education, healthcare, and farming, Daniel Björkegren, an assistant professor at Columbia University, said at the Rest of World event last week.
“In the low-income context, there’s a lot of concern about being dependent on the U.S. for frontier intelligence,” he said. “American models are also very tuned for American workloads, but when you take those same models and try to deploy them in remote parts of the world, often they don’t work so well.”
Users, particularly businesses, switch models “when new capabilities and lower prices emerge,” Björkegren said. But “one enduring question is, how easy is it to switch?”

articles.title: Continuous accountability for Verified bots
articles.summary:
Continuous accountability for Verified bots
A driver’s license tells you who someone is and that they passed a driving test, not whether they’ll drive responsibly in the future. The same is true for bots: verifying who operates it creates accountability, but trust depends on what it does next. A known bot can still ignore website preferences, overwhelm origins, or evade controls. It’s not always malicious — often it’s just a misconfiguration or a bug.
As we described in a previous blog post on bot behavior, we strive to verify two questions: “Are you who you say you are?” and “Can we trust you?” To be a Cloudflare Verified Bot, you broadly need to meet three criteria:
- Identify yourself accurately and securely
- Do only what you say you will do
- Don’t engage in abusive behavior
Bots use Web Bot Auth to sign requests that establish their identity, which BotBase then catalogues in an open format. With identification addressed, our focus shifts to the second cardinal rule of Verified bots: thou shalt do no harm.
Today we introduce a system to evaluate and report when Verified bot behavior starts to deviate from this rule, ensuring that the answer to “Can we trust you?” remains “Yes.”
This is where the distinction between risk and trust becomes important:
- Risk describes the likelihood that a particular request or point-in-time action may be harmful, and it can change from one moment to the next.
- Trust is built over time through repeated and consistent behavior.

articles.title: Africa's jobs problem is bigger than unemployment
articles.summary:
Africa’s unemployment rate looks relatively low by global standards. In 2025, the continent’s rate stood at 6.3%. But that figure tells only part of the story. More than a third of employed Africans live in working poverty; they are employed but live below the poverty line of $2.15 a day. Most workers are informally employed, and fewer than one in five people have social protection coverage.
Having a job does not necessarily mean earning enough to support a household, escaping poverty, or having protection when things go wrong. To understand the African labour market, it is necessary to look beyond unemployment to examine the type of work people do and how secure their livelihoods are.
Most Africans work, but most work informally
The International Labour Organisation (ILO) defines employment rate as the share of the working-age population who have worked at least an hour for pay or profit during a reference period of one week or seven days.
Under this definition, a person can be considered employed even if they work for only a short period. The measure captures whether someone has work, but it does not, on its own, establish whether that work provides a secure livelihood.
Africa has a growing working-age population, with more young people entering the labour market each year. The World Bank estimates that Sub-Saharan Africa needs to create around 15 million jobs annually to absorb its growing working-age population. articles.title: TSE aprova regras para vincular canais de WhatsApp a campanhas eleitorais
articles.summary:
O Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) aprovou, por unanimidade, nesta sexta-feira (16), novas regras para determinar quando canais de mensagens instantâneas, como os do WhatsApp, estão vinculados a campanhas eleitorais. A resolução estabelece seis critérios para identificar essa relação e determina que os canais enquadrados nessa condição sejam registrados na Justiça Eleitoral.
A proposta, relatada pelo ministro André Mendonça, altera a resolução que regulamenta a propaganda eleitoral. Entre os critérios estão o uso de recursos financeiros ou suporte técnico de campanhas, a divulgação dos canais em perfis oficiais, a atuação coordenada de apoiadores e a orientação sobre os conteúdos publicados.
A norma também esclarece que o apoio político espontâneo não caracteriza, por si só, um vínculo com uma candidatura. A identificação da relação precisa ser sustentada por elementos objetivamente verificáveis.
A aprovação ocorre após uma sequência de decisões conflitantes no próprio TSE envolvendo o canal Exército do Lula, administrado pelo deputado federal André Janones (Rede/MG), e um pedido da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) para retirar a página do ar.
Quais critérios definem o vínculo com uma campanha?
A resolução estabelece seis critérios que não precisam ser cumpridos simultaneamente. Ou seja, a comprovação de apenas um deles pode ser suficiente para caracterizar a ligação entre o canal e uma candidatura.

Der Baustein-Ansatz aktueller Tools wie Flora oder Magnific Spaces dreht das Prinzip um: Die Arbeit lebt nicht in Chats, sondern auf einer Arbeitsfläche.
Den Anfang macht die Idee. articles.title: Building trust in AI agents: A production-ready evaluation framework with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Building trust in AI agents: A production-ready evaluation framework with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
The North Star
Every organization racing to deploy AI agents faces the same reckoning: an agent that demos beautifully can quietly degrade in production, and by the time a human notices, the trust is already broken. Where traditional software fails loudly, agents fail softly. They return an answer that looks confident, reads fluently, and is wrong. When that answer drives a real business decision, the cost is not a broken feature. It’s a broken relationship with the user.
That’s the quality problem at its core. The challenge is therefore not building agents that work once, but proving they keep working, at scale, across every sub-agent, every workflow, and every release. The teams that win the agent era will be the ones who treat quality not as a final QA step but as the operating system of the agent itself: continuously measured, automatically defended, and improved with every interaction. In this post, we show how we built a continuous quality loop for production-ready agentic solutions at scale using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

articles.title: Vuyani Jarana: How a boy fascinated by radios became a champion of rural connectivity
articles.summary: Vuyani Jarana, CEO of Ilitha Telecoms, is taking affordable broadband into underserved townships and rural communities. In a conversation with PHATHISANI MOYO, he explains why connecting homes is only the beginning, and how education, healthcare and local businesses could turn internet access into lasting economic opportunity. As a boy growing up in Eastern Cape Province, Vuyani Jarana was fascinated by the voices coming out of a radio. He and his friends wondered how people could speak from inside a box, so they would open discarded sets and try to fix them. “We wanted to understand how it worked, even though there were no people inside it,” recalls the chief executive officer (CEO) of Ilitha Telecommunications , a township and rural broadband provider founded in 2019. Television was another attraction. One household in his village had a television and a generator, turning its lounge into an informal cinema where children gathered after football to watch movies. The room often became chaotic as they took over the entire space, Jarana told TechCabal in an interview on Monday. Today, the former Vodacom executive, a mobile network connecting millions across Africa, is building broadband networks for communities like the one where he grew up. Ilitha wants to connect 600,000 homes, backed by R500 million ($30.4 million) in funding from Absa Corporate and Investment Banking (CIB) . articles.title: Meta’s new terms may allow it to train AI on news sites for free
articles.summary:
Meta’s new terms appear to give it permission to crawl and scrape websites “associated” with the businesses that use its platforms — including online publishers, according to a report from Nieman Lab. The new terms, which go into effect on October 30th, say Meta can use this outside content to “develop, improve, research,” and “train” its AI products.
Meta’s new terms may allow it to train AI on news sites for free
The new policy allows Meta to crawl all websites ‘associated’ with a business account.
While Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts says that the company is just “consolidating” its commercial and self-serve ad terms, legal experts tell Nieman Lab that this could allow Meta “to argue its commercial terms supersede other blocking instructions,” like a site’s robots.txt file. That could potentially allow Meta to bypass a licensing agreement and freely train its AI models on content posted by online publishers.
The new policy applies to business accounts that promote their content across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger:

articles.title: OpenAI suspende el lanzamiento de un nuevo modelo de IA debido a preocupaciones de seguridad
articles.summary:
OpenAI ha cancelado el lanzamiento de GPT-6.1 Astra, su modelo más potente, el cual estaba previsto para octubre, porque sus pruebas internas lo dejaron por debajo de lo que se esperaba. Saachi Jain, responsable de sistemas de seguridad de la empresa americana, lo explica comentando que el modelo había mejorado en “pereza”, pero no estaba donde ellos esperaban en cuanto a “mantenerse dentro del alcance y la autorización”.
Según cuenta Jain, GPT-6.1 Astra engañaba más que su predecesor, haciendo que no siempre contestara con veracidad qué había hecho y qué no; también continuaba con una tarea sin pedir ningún tipo de permiso e incluso, a veces, usaba herramientas externas sin excesivo cuidado. Todo esto quiere decir que llevaba a cabo acciones que nadie le había autorizado y no siempre lo contaba bien.

articles.title: This is the AMD Helios HPE Juniper QFX5252 Switch Tray at OCP 2026

At OCP 2026, we saw something that looked absolutely awesome. Walking by the HPE booth, we saw an AMD Helios tray set up and open on the show floor. It stopped me in my tracks, so I thought folks would like to see it.
This is the AMD Helios HPE Juniper QFX5252 Switch Tray at OCP 2026
Oftentimes, when we open up huge switches, we see a lot of internal PCB. This is totally different since it is a double-wide tray with side-by-side switches and lots of copper.
You can see the HPE QFX5252 label on the front latch, which is huge. Because there is so much connectivity on the back, and the back panel is long and needs to blind mate, the insertion force required for a switch tray like this into the Helios rack is significant. As a result, these levers are very long.
Since this is two big switch chips in a 1OU tray, it needs to be liquid cooled. You can see the internal liquid cooling manifolds distributing liquid to the various blocks.
There are two switch chips inside, which are Broadcom Tomahawk 6 102.6T switches. At first, you might wonder why these are not Broadcom Tomahawk Ultra chips, since that might make sense for a scale-up architecture. The current generation Tomahawk Ultra is a 112G PAM4 SerDes switch (so 512 lanes of PAM4-112G.) That is not enough for Helios which is using 224G PAM4 SerDes. As a result, these need to be Tomahawk 6.
Now, the next part is very different. AMD and HPE-Juniper are not just slinging Tomahawk 6 on some PCBs and calling it a day. You will notice …

- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. Un grupo de investigadores españoles ha ido a mirarlo.

Probaron las versiones web y las apps de Android, y su estudio, aceptado en el Privacy Enhancing Technologies Symposium (PETS), concluye algo que no encaja con la imagen de confidente: los nueve contactan con al menos un servicio de publicidad o de seguimiento de terceros.
¿Qué sale de tu chat y adónde va?
Seis de las nueve versiones web (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Grok, Perplexity y Mistral) y tres de las ocho apps de Android revelan a terceras direcciones de conversación, títulos, mensajes o capturas de pantalla, a menudo junto a identificadores persistentes del usuario. articles.title: Kids are outsmarting social media bans. That’s not a problem we need to solve.
articles.summary:
Kids are outsmarting social media bans. That’s not a problem we need to solve.
Age gates can be staggeringly counterproductive, pushing kids to darker corners of the web. Closing loopholes will only make things worse.
Social media bans are stacking up. In July, France joined Australia in restricting minors from accessing social media—barring children under 15 from major platforms, before the ban was blocked by the country’s top court on human rights grounds. The UK aims to forbid kids under 16 from accessing Facebook, TikTok, and other platforms in early 2027, and the EU has announced its own plan to prohibit social media for kids under 15.
But early lessons from Australia, which enacted a ban in 2024, show that these sorts of age restrictions are easily circumvented. A study published earlier this year found that four in five teens under 16 made their way onto barred platforms. Teens have successfully explored many tactics for bypassing bans, from using a sibling’s face for ID to drawing fake facial hair.
Some proponents of bans have called for an increased focus on enforcement that blocks these workarounds. But circumvention is a signal, not a nuisance or something to be simply deterred. The fact that kids are actively looking for ways to outwit the bans highlights their limitations. Social media bans suppress kids’ access to information, including information that’s essential to their development, identity formation, and socialization, especially during adolescence. Worse,…

articles.title: Microsoft Commits Maia to Multi-Gigawatt Inference, and Its Efficiency Metric Draws Questions
articles.summary:
Microsoft will scale its Azure Maia family to multi-gigawatt deployments starting in 2027, making Maia "the primary inference system for Microsoft products and services." The architecture behind that commitment is unusually specific about data movement. The efficiency claim leading the announcement is not, and practitioners have said so.
Maia 200 is already in production, serving Microsoft Copilot and the MAI team, with GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Foundry to follow by the end of the year. It is deployed across the United States, Europe, and Australia, and Microsoft says it delivers up to 1.7 times more tokens per watt for built-in AI in Teams and Copilot than leading GPU infrastructure. Maia 300 begins production deployments in 2027.
Maia 300 is inference-first, aimed at long-context, memory-intensive, and decode-heavy work rather than training, which neither announcement mentions. Each accelerator carries eight HBM4 stacks, providing 288 GB and 18 TB/s within a 950-watt TDP. A rack holds 96 accelerators in 167 kW across 24 four-accelerator trays, reaching 27.6 TB of HBM and 1.7 PB/s aggregate. Compute chiplets are built on TSMC N2P, with memory-controller and I/O functions on separate dies, which Microsoft says raises compute FLOPs by 36% and contributes to 2.5 times the memory bandwidth and roughly twice the HBM bandwidth per watt of Maia 200. La más famosa es la cinta de los años 90 protagonizada por Jean-Claude Van Damme pero, dejando de lado su gran componente nostálgico, deja mucho que desear.

Distanciados entre sí, se ven arrastrados de nuevo al combate cuando la misteriosa Chun-Li los recluta para el próximo Torneo "World Warrior", un enfrentamiento brutal de puños, destino y furia.

articles.title: Microsoft Patches Two Dozen RCE Flaws in Office
articles.summary:
Hot on the heels of its record Patch Tuesday rollout, Microsoft on Thursday announced patches for over 30 new vulnerabilities.
Most of the new fixes address security defects in the Office suite. Two dozen of them patch high-severity remote code execution (RCE) flaws, including half a dozen bugs that could be targeted via the Preview Pane.
In most cases, exploitation requires an attacker to send a specially crafted file, such as a malicious document, and convince the recipient to open it.
Buffer overflow issues are blamed for most of the RCEs, with several defects being off-by-one, use-after-free, path traversal, and numeric truncation errors.
Word received the majority of patches, with only a few rolled out for Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and SharePoint.
In addition to RCE flaws, Microsoft fixed multiple information disclosure bugs and a security bypass issue in the Office suite.
Additionally, it resolved a denial-of-service (DoS) defect in ASP.NET Core, an elevation of privilege in Identity Web, and an information disclosure in Authentication Library (MSAL) for Node.js.
According to Microsoft, none of the newly resolved issues have been exploited in the wild as a zero-day.
On Thursday, Microsoft also updated dozens of advisories initially published on October 13 to notify customers that security updates have been released for Office LTSC for Mac 2021 and 2024, and for Office 365 for Mac.

Every time an AI agent has to trawl Slack threads, Jira tickets and old pull requests to piece together something a company already knows, the customer pays for that work again. Uvi, an Israeli startup that emerged from stealth on Wednesday with $7.5 million in seed funding from investors including CT Innovations, Cardumen, Mana VC and 91 Ventures, says this repeated context-gathering is quietly inflating the cost of running agents on frontier models.
The firm says in-house agents built on frontier models, connected directly to six company systems, cost roughly eight times more than they needed in internal testing, mostly because of repeated context gathering rather than actual reasoning.
Developers are paying for amnesia
Uvi co-founder and CEO Gilad Salinger tells The New Stack that models are rented, but context is owned.
“Developers are paying frontier prices for amnesia,” Salinger says. “Every quarter there’s a new model that is faster and cheaper, and every quarter the company’s memory of why it built things the way it did stays exactly where it was: in people’s heads, in old tickets, in Slack threads nobody will read again.”

As a result, businesses continue to face an AI skills gap: not just a shortage of technical expertise, but a shortage of the human capability needed to prove the return on large-scale AI investments is mounting.

The technology in the new Tesla Roadster that allowed it to fly was developed with sister company SpaceX.

And while the demonstration was spectacular and jaw-dropping, the reality is Tesla will face a long winding road to achieve road legality.

articles.title: Backdooring Open-Weight AI Models - Schneier on Security
articles.summary:
Backdooring Open-Weight AI Models
This is a problem:
Any open model whose weights have been edited can carry a backdoor, whether it’s a task-specific fine-tune, a merged adapter or an abliterated build. We have abliterated models in the title because it’s the most popular reason people download modified weights without verifying what’s inside. Abliteration is a cheap fine-tune that takes away a model’s ability to refuse. You find the direction in the weights that carries “no” and subtract it. The model then answers things a safety-tuned version would turn down. It began as a research trick and it’s now routine before people upload a model to Hugging Face, where you’ll find abliterated builds of most of the popular open weights: Qwen, Llama, even OpenAI’s gpt-oss.
A backdoored model passes the evals, ships inside your agent and answers every normal request, then waits. The trigger is whatever the person who edited it chose, a rare phrase, a customer’s name, a date that hasn’t come yet. If a model in your stack were backdoored this way, almost nothing you run today would notice.
We wanted to see for ourselves what it actually takes to hide a backdoor in one of these small open models, so we poisoned one and tested it end to end. Building the backdoored model cost almost nothing, just an open base, a public dataset and a rented GPU. The model ships carrying only a URL to a remote payload, so whoever controls that URL can swap the behaviour months after deployment without retrain…

OpenAI has disclosed two incidents in which internal AI models, asked only to look up public figures, instead broke into the live systems hosting that data.
The reports, published on October 15, are the latest in a run of misalignment disclosures OpenAI started after its models compromised Hugging Face in July.
OpenAI has since disclosed several other incidents, including models probing government websites for vulnerabilities, attempting to exploit SQL injection flaws, and searching GitHub for leaked API keys during training.
What marks these two cases out is how ordinary the starting point was. Neither was an offensive-security exercise. In both, the model was given a routine job — fetch a published statistic from a public source — and turned to exploitation by itself, then said nothing about it in its final answer.
OpenAI said it caught both incidents by running its misalignment monitor back over earlier training and evaluation activity, and rated each critical. The company has since taken steps to prevent similar incidents.
Disclosed the same day was a third, separate case in which an unrelated model spent cryptocurrency from a wallet it did not control.
All three of the newly disclosed incidents occurred in June and were discovered in investigations conducted in the following months.

E Ink’s new Kaleido 4 technology might finally lead to color ereaders that are worth buying
Let there be light
- E Ink has announced the next generation of its color ereader screens
- Dubbed Kaleido 4, this technology promises improved clarity, less graininess, and double the colors
- So far, it's only been announced for a single ereader, but it's sure to come to others
Hot take: I don’t think color ereaders are very good in general. The colors themselves are muted, and typically — such as with E Ink’s Kaleido 3 tech — they make the screen darker and grainier even when just viewing text. They generally cost a premium, too. As such, I’d always pick a black-and-white ereader for standard books, and a tablet (or actual paper) for anything heavy on color.
But E Ink might soon win me over to color ereaders, as it just announced a new Kaleido 4 display that it claims is brighter than Kaleido 3 and delivers “greater clarity, while reducing the perception of screen graininess.”
If that's true, normal text might actually look up to the standards it does on black-and-white e-readers.

articles.title: AWS Introduces Strands Decider 2B and Strands Box for AI Agent Development

AWS has introduced two open-source projects for AI agent development: Strands Decider 2B, a small model designed to make decisions within agent workflows, and Strands Box, a sandbox for controlling agent execution. Both projects address different aspects of building agents that use tools, execute code, and interact with external systems.
Strands Decider 2B is a two-billion-parameter model designed to select between predefined options rather than generate lengthy text responses. It supports tasks such as model routing, tool selection, classification, guardrails, and context management. Instead of asking a general-purpose language model to generate an answer, developers can provide a set of choices and receive a decision with confidence scores.
The model is based on Qwen3.5-2B, with its language-model head replaced by a pointer head that scores candidate answers. It uses a rank-16 LoRA adapter for fine-tuning. AWS has released the model weights, training data, and scripts, allowing developers to run and modify the model locally.
According to AWS, Strands Decider 2B achieved a median decision latency of approximately 115 milliseconds on an NVIDIA RTX 3090 and 153 milliseconds for small tasks on an Apple M3 MacBook. The company also evaluated the model using JevBench, reporting 72.3% accuracy across 231 public tasks for its v19 checkpoint. Developers can install the strands-decider package and use its command-line interface or integrate the model into Strands agents.

articles.title: This implant can restore sight for patients with macular degeneration
articles.summary:
This implant can restore sight for patients with macular degeneration
The PRIMA system lets people with advanced AMD read and do crosswords. Here’s how it works.
More than 5 million people around the world with age-related macular degeneration (AMD) experience atrophy in their retinas. And until now, no treatment could restore their vision. The PRIMA system, which was approved in Europe in July and is awaiting FDA clearance in the US, changes that. It combines a retinal implant with camera-equipped eyeglasses to improve sight in patients who develop a blind spot in the middle of their vision due to advanced AMD. After training sessions, more than 80% of recipients were able to read, do crosswords, and use their phones.
Developed by the California-based Science Corporation, the system takes advantage of the fact that AMD doesn’t damage all retinal circuitry; only photoreceptors—the cells that convert light into an electrical signal—die off. PRIMA’s implant mimics those cells and transmits visual information directly to healthy eye circuitry and on to the brain. “We’re leveraging all of the body’s own natural functions to process and transmit the information,” says Frank Brodie, an ophthalmologist at the University of California, San Francisco, and Science Corp.'s chief medical officer for ophthalmology.

En otros caos, por el contrario, simplemente sirven para cerrar alguna subtramas que había quedado abierta durante el metraje. Incluso hay veces que se utilizan como gag sin mayores pretensiones para sacar una última sonrisa a los fans más pacientes.
La duda sobre qué podría ocurrir con Street Fighter era más que lógica dado que es un nuevo reinicio de la icónica saga de videojuegos de peleas. Investors do that work because they are making a long-term bet on your abilities.
However, the same isn’t true in reverse. In two decades supporting founders as they raise, I have found the majority could tell me everything about their own metrics, ambition for the business or ideal team hires, but very little about the people they approached for funding.
So, why is this? DocSend’s research on pre-seed rounds found founders contacted an average of 71 investors to close a round. articles.title: Six years after Stripe, Paystack is learning to keep money
articles.summary: In October 2020, Stripe agreed to buy Paystack, a Lagos startup that helped businesses take payments online, for $200 million , the largest acquisition of a Nigerian startup. At the time, Paystack had 60,000 customers. Stripe said the deal would fund new products and help pull Africa’s scattered payments market together and that Paystack would keep running on its own. Shola Akinlade, its chief executive, promised more countries, more payment channels and more services. Six years after the acquisition, he has fulfilled that promise. In 2020, Paystack made money by taking a cut each time a business collected payment online, a model that needs scale. It charges 1.5% plus ₦100 per transaction, capped at ₦2,000, so a ₦10,000 order earns it ₦250, about 19 cents. This model earns income only when money moves; unlike a bank that holds customers’ money, it can lend or invest it at a higher rate than it pays for it, and that income keeps coming for as long as the balances stay, with or without transactions. Brazil’s Nubank shows how well this works. It ended 2025 with $41.9 billion in deposits, paid 87% of the interbank rate to fund itself, and made $2.9 billion. Worldwide, interest made up 46% of payments revenue in 2024, according to McKinsey. Six years on, the company Stripe bought has changed shape. articles.title: Veritas expands its anti-counterfeit chip to jewelry, trophies, and fragrance bottles | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Counterfeits of luxury goods are a major problem for fashion houses. Counterfeiters are getting better at replicating brands’ marks and passing off dupes, known as “superfakes,” as genuine items. A startup called Veritas wants to tackle the problem with its own chip that verifies goods.
Veritas was founded by Luci Holland, a former Tesla technical product manager who also has a background in design and art. Its chip is built to be easily inserted into products without damaging them. Brands can use it to verify whether a product is the real deal, and customers can show a certificate of ownership through the company’s app.
Holland said other approaches are easier to defeat, because a digital record can be reproduced through a copied QR code or static NFC link.
“Our approach combines secure, authenticated chip responses with integration into the product itself. Our chip generates a secure response with each tap and includes a tamper-detection wire. We make the connection between the object and its digital identity part of the proof,” Holland said.
The Veritas founder told TechCrunch over email that the company has just introduced the second version of its chip, which works on metal surfaces and can be scanned through glass.
“The next-generation chip is ready for production and supports a broader range of applications, including jewelry, trophies, hard-surface products, and glass objects such as fragrance bottles,” Holland said. “Alongside our garment integrations, this gives bra…

For Solidigm, leaving that space idle limits sales. The company sells every SSD it makes, and more NAND output would let it supply more drives.
The Dalian plant is the only factory in the world producing Solidigm's 192-layer floating-gate 3D NAND. That memory goes into SSDs for AI, enterprise and hyperscale data centers.

Un colis trop volumineux, un livreur qui vous a manqué, quelques euros de frais à régler pour choisir un nouveau créneau… L’arnaque au faux SMS de livraison circule depuis des années, mais elle revient en force à chaque période d’achats, et le Black Friday approche. Ses ressorts, eux, restent méconnus.
Pour les comprendre, nous avons cliqué sur le lien d’un de ces messages, depuis un téléphone de test et avec de fausses informations, en documentant chaque étape. Voici ce que nous avons vu, ce que les escrocs récupèrent réellement, et les bons réflexes à adopter, même si vous avez déjà cliqué.
Le SMS : tout est fait pour que vous cliquiez vite
Le message tient en deux lignes : « Bonjour, c’est le livreur, votre colis ne rentrait pas dans la boîte aux lettres », suivi d’un lien pour choisir un point relais. Pourtant, quatre détails doivent alerter :
- L’expéditeur : un numéro de mobile classique en 06 ou 07, et non le nom d’un transporteur.
- L’urgence : un ton pressé, une livraison « en attente », un colis bientôt renvoyé.
- Le lien : une adresse qui imite celle du transporteur, avec un tiret ou un mot en trop.
- Le contexte : le message arrive sans qu’on ait rien commandé, ou au moment précis où l’on attend un colis, ce qui le rend d’autant plus crédible.

Grundlage dafür ist die EU-Verordnung eIDAS 2.0, die jeden Mitgliedstaat verpflichtet, seinen Bürgern eine solche Wallet anzubieten. Die Bundesregierung plant dazu entsprechende Regeln im Digitale Identitätengesetz (DIdG), über den Gesetzentwurf stimmt der Bundestag voraussichtlich am Donnerstag ab.
Die Deutsche Kreditwirtschaft (DK), als Interessenvertretung der Banken und Sparkassen, fordert nun Nachschärfungen im Gesetz. Zwar begrüßen die Banken, dass Kunden sich künftig per Wallet geldwäscherechtlich identifizieren können, wenn sie ein Konto eröffnen. Die Institute fordern jedoch, klar festzulegen, dass es ausreicht, die vom Wallet–Verfahren bereitgestellten Daten zu speichern, also dass eine Ausweiskopie weder erforderlich noch technisch umsetzbar ist. Ohne diese Präzisierung könnten Banken sonst vorsichtshalber zusätzliche Nachweise verlangen, wodurch der Vorteil einer schnellen, papierlosen Kontoeröffnung verloren gehen könnte.
Außerdem müsse das Gesetz klarer regeln, wann Banken eine fremde Wallet akzeptieren müssen, wer bei technischen Fehlern haftet und welche Daten ihnen zur Betrugsabwehr zur Verfügung stehen.

At the time of writing, the Apple Canada website showed an expected shipping time of Jan. 26 across both colour options and all storage options for the phone.
Of course, that’s just Apple’s online store. It’s possible you might be able to find the Duo at physical locations once the phone launches on Oct. 23, both at Apple and other retailers like Best Buy, or even at carrier stores. But your mileage may vary with that.
The limited stock shouldn’t come as much of a surprise. Reports leading up to and even after the iPhone Duo’s unveiling consistently noted Apple was struggling with production issues that would limit the launch supply.

articles.title: Googlebook review: Android on a laptop is still Android
articles.summary:
Android was designed for phones, but that hasn’t stopped Google from trying to adapt the OS and its apps to larger machines over the years. Googlebooks are just the latest attempt after tablets, Chromebooks, and foldables induced little change in how people interact with Android software. These new Android-powered laptops are designed to pick up where the web-focused ChromeOS left off, offering premium hardware and native support for Android apps.
Google sees Googlebooks as an alternative to Windows and macOS, but these platforms are entrenched with decades of software and UI conventions that keep users locked in. Googlebooks have to offer something very special to steal users away from either of the dominant operating systems.
For devoted Android phone users, there are some cool things in Googlebook OS, but the Android roots of these machines are impossible to miss. Sometimes it feels like using a Chromebook, and sometimes it feels like using a giant phone. It almost never feels like using a premium laptop, and that’s the problem.
OEMs pulling their weight
While there were a few premium Chromebooks, the platform was really only successful in the budget segment. With Googlebooks, the company is almost conspicuously ignoring lower-cost options. And as most of the lineup clocks in at well over a thousand dollars, Googlebooks are not just a new take on budget-oriented Chromebooks.

After a few revisions of his position on AI-assisted contributions to the Linux kernel, Linus Torvalds has posted his own first LLM-assisted patch. The development branch purports to fix an old issue with massive cache contention when many CPUs are reading the same file — a scenario potentially encountered when using shared libraries, databases, and web servers. Several developers had already made attempts over the years at fixing the issue, all with varied results, none quite ideal as an all-encompassing solution.
Torvalds posted his own draft for solving the problem in early 2024, and has used it on his own laptop since that time. However, he recently took the plunge and decided to "try to actually solve this thing using an LLM." He's now posted his solution in a development branch, and claims that he's seen a 23x performance improvement in a dedicated synthetic benchmark, though he notes that actual real-world impact will be far less significant, as "no real load" will witness those figures. If we had to guess, this improvement would benefit server workloads far more than desktop machines.

Winners & losers: It's a depressingly common sight to see tickets for concerts, shows, and other events getting snapped up en masse before appearing on reseller sites with huge markups. It's why Washington DC introduced a bill limiting how much resellers can raise the price of tickets, but the marketplaces are now suing the District of Columbia to block this law.
The DC council passed the Restricting Egregious Scalping Against Live Entertainment Amendment (RESALE) Act in June. Set to become law on January 1, 2027, it ensures that tickets purchased for shows can't be resold for more than 10% of the original price, including fees and taxes. It also limits the service fee that a resale marketplace can charge to 10% of that same original price. Tickets to most sporting events and movie tickets are exempt.
That sounds like a law that would be welcomed by everyone other than scalpers profiting from the tickets. But the resale sites themselves are also unhappy about it, unsurprisingly.
Four of these companies – SeatGeek, Vivid Seats, Gametime and TickPick – are so against the RESALE Act that they're suing to stop it from going into effect.
Brian Berry, Executive Director of the Ticket Policy Forum (TPF), a trade association of online ticket marketplaces, claims the law will simply drive ticket scams into shady, unregulated areas, subjecting fans to greater risks from street-side scams and increased fraud.

articles.summary:
“Finalement, le futur a bien des voitures volantes” : avec SpaceX, Tesla fait quitter le sol à son nouveau Roadster
Près de neuf ans après sa première apparition, le Roadster de série est enfin là. Il a des propulseurs à gaz froid conçus avec SpaceX, il saute par-dessus un camion et sa version la plus radicale passe de 0 à 96 km/h en moins de 0,6 seconde. Son prix reste inconnu, et l'autonomie promise en 2017 a fondu de moitié.
Dans la nuit de jeudi à vendredi, heure française, Elon Musk a dévoilé la deuxième génération du Tesla Roadster sur un site d'essais de SpaceX à McGregor, au Texas. L'événement était prévu le 1er octobre, puis reporté à cause de la météo. Le spectacle a été à la hauteur de l'attente. La sportive électrique a gravi une rampe incurvée jusqu'à rouler la tête en bas, plaquée par ses ventilateurs d'aspiration. Elle s'en est ensuite arrachée, a pivoté en l'air et s'est reposée sur le bitume.
Dans une seconde séquence, elle a franchi d'un bond un Cybercab, un Cybertruck, un Semi, un Model Y et une Model 3 alignés.
Trois versions du Tesla Roadster, dont une sur invitation

Fitness functions signal when a system drifts; comprehension confirms people still grasp what they are modifying; boundaries define where independent change can happen; platforms turn safe practices into repeatable defaults; and organizational design ensures those boundaries actually survive contact with reality.

That infection mechanism was called Aladdin and surfaced due to a collection of marketing files and documents leaked from the Intellexa surveillance company that researchers studied and corroborated with technical details from forensic investigations.
Unlike Alladin, AdFection was caught in real attacks and linked to Israeli firm Discovere-Tech, described by Citizen Lab as " a bridge between mercenary spyware companies and the advertising ecosystem."

articles.title: Gartner: The quantum threat is already behind schedule
articles.summary:
Gartner: The quantum threat is already behind schedule
Why post-quantum cryptography requires action now
For years, quantum computing lived in a strange place in the cybersecurity conversation: important enough to worry about, but sufficiently distant to leave for another day. When we asked CISO what's keeping them up at night, quantum computing rarely made the top five. It still feels distant, theoretical, someone else's problem for 2030-something.
That calculation is starting to look wrong.
Director Analyst within the ITL Application and Data Security research team at Gartner.
Gartner predicts that by 2030, advances in quantum computing will make conventional asymmetric cryptography unsafe to use. Four years away sounds like breathing room. It isn't. Replacing the cryptography embedded across a modern technology estate isn't a patch cycle. It's a multi-year transformation touching applications, infrastructure, identity systems, suppliers and developers all at once.
The clock is already running. Most organizations just haven't noticed it started or don’t appreciate how little time they really have.
This was never really a technology question
Quantum innovation is moving at pace with IBM, Amazon and Google publishing roadmaps or breakthroughs on error correction and qubit stability. Taken together, they tell a consistent story: the timeline to a cryptographically relevant quantum computer is shrinking, not stretching.

articles.title: Grafana Applies SLOs and Error Budgets to AI Agent Behaviour
articles.summary:
Grafana Labs is proposing a familiar reliability engineering approach for one of the less familiar problems in modern software: how to measure whether an AI agent is actually behaving well. In a recent article, the company describes using evaluations, service-level objectives (SLOs) and error budgets to turn behaviours such as hallucination, task fulfilment, toxicity, and cost into measurable targets that can be monitored over time.
The idea addresses a fundamental limitation of conventional application observability. Traditional metrics can tell engineers that an agent responded quickly, encountered no technical errors, and consumed a certain number of tokens, but none necessarily indicate whether its answer was correct, grounded in available information, or useful to the user. Grafana's approach is to evaluate the behaviour itself and turn the result into an SLI that can be measured against an SLO.
The first step is evaluation. An evaluation examines an agent interaction and determines whether it met a particular behavioural criterion. Grafana describes examples including whether a response was grounded in its supplied context, fulfilled the user's request, contained toxic content, exposed personal information, or succumbed to prompt injection. Evaluations can use another language model as a judge, but deterministic checks such as regular expressions can also be used where the behaviour can be identified without an LLM.

Dans les faits, le célèbre milliardaire à la tête de SpaceX ne ment pas et cela dépend beaucoup du modèle et de la région. Tesla se défend d’ailleurs au sujet de la version Rocket en affirmant qu’elle « peut ne pas être disponible dans toutes les régions ». Pour un acheteur français, la question se pose donc très concrètement : aura-t-il le droit de s’en servir ?
Aujourd’hui, aucune version n’est autorisée
Pour vous faire une réponse courte aujourd’hui : la réponse est non et cela concerne toutes les variantes. Le Roadster ne sera pas produit avant 2028 et Tesla n’a annoncé aucune démarche d’homologation européenne. Or, en France comme dans le reste de l’Union européenne, une voiture doit être réceptionnée, c’est-à-dire homologuée, avant d’obtenir une carte grise.

articles.title: Una estudiante de 17 años ha convertido bidones industriales en barriles de lluvia. Su objetivo: que 170.000 litros no acaben en ríos y acuíferos
articles.summary:
La escorrentía es el flujo de agua de lluvia, nieve o deshielo que circula sobre o a través de la superficie terrestre cuando la precipitación supera la capacidad de evaporación e infiltración del suelo. Es un proceso natural en el ciclo del agua y positivo en muchísimos aspectos porque es la principal fuente de agua que llena los ríos, lagos y embalses.
Sin embargo, cuando este flujo de agua avanza por el terreno también puede recoger y transportar basura, pesticidas, aceites o metales pesados que pueden llegar a contaminar el agua. Hay muchas maneras de evitar que este tipo de escorrentía llegue a aguas locales, y tampoco se necesita mucho. De hecho, una adolescente de Texas ha convertido bidones industriales desechados en barriles de lluvia. Según sus propios cálculos, estos han evitado que unos 170.000 litros de escorrentía lleguen a los cursos de agua locales. El proyecto de Kaitlyn Tran le ha valido uno de los Premios Gloria Barron de este año para Jóvenes Héroes.
Lo interesante de todo no es el método con el que lo ha hecho, sino que ha movilizado iniciativas medioambientales en torno a estos barriles en su localidad, una región especialmente sensible por grandes lluvias.
Por qué importa. Cuando la lluvia cae sobre tejados, carreteras y aparcamientos, no puede filtrarse en el suelo. En su lugar, se precipita hacia los desagües pluviales, arrastrando aceite, basura y residuos de fertilizantes hacia ríos, lagos y acuíferos. Esto es motivo de especial preocupación en Ceda…

articles.title: Critical BlockStrap flaw lets hackers run code on Magento servers

Researchers warn that hackers could soon exploit a maximum-severity vulnerability (CVE-2026-103849) affecting Magento and Adobe Commerce, potentially allowing them to execute arbitrary PHP code on store servers.
According to e-commerce security firm Sansec, attacks leveraging the vulnerability, dubbed BlockStrap, have not yet been observed, but threat actors are expected to find a way to exploit it.
The researchers based their assessment on identifying four potential attack paths involving CVE-2026-103849 in less than 24 hours.
The flaw impacts September versions of Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source through 2.4.9 and Adobe Commerce B2B through 1.5.3.
The security firm warned that Adobe’s “priority 2” rating of this flaw does not reflect the danger and urgency in this case, despite the more complex attack path.
“The attack path is complex, but anyone with an AI agent can reverse-engineer the patch into working exploits in a relatively short time,” stated Sansec states.
“That is why we question Adobe's priority 2 rating (patch within 30 days). StyleSmuggler went from a priority 1 hotfix to mass exploitation in three days, and BlockStrap is of similar complexity.”
Adobe’s bulletin, published on October 13, describes the flaw as an improper neutralization of special elements used in a template engine, leading to arbitrary code execution.

Tous les Roadster ne seront pas concernés. Tesla prévoit trois versions à la réservation : la Performance, présentée comme « prête pour la route », se passe de propulseurs et mise sur un système d’aspiration par ventilateurs ; la Thrust, « prête pour la course », ajoute des propulseurs à gaz froid à l’arrière pour passer sous la seconde de 0 à 96 km/h ; la Rocket, « prête pour les airs » et la seule capable de voler, en compte dix répartis autour de la carrosserie.

articles.title: Experiment shows liquid metal TIM doesn’t dry out; it turns solid — two-year electron microscope test finds gallium bonds with copper coolers, and nickel plating keeps the layer about 10 times thinner
articles.summary:
Experiment shows liquid metal TIM doesn’t dry out; it turns solid — two-year electron microscope test finds gallium bonds with copper coolers, and nickel plating keeps the layer about 10 times thinner
Liquid metal’s hardened layer conducts heat about a quarter as well as the copper it replaces.
YouTuber hardware enthusiast and Thermal Grizzly boss der8auer tested a two-year-old liquid metal thermal interface material (TIM) application with an electron microscope in his new video, discovering that it doesn’t dry out. Instead, the gallium bonds with the copper in a reaction to form a solid compound. On copper, that layer’s heat conduction performance is about one-quarter of the bare metal’s, and nickel plating keeps it about 10 times thinner.
His test showed the TIM as liquid after one hour, no liquid visible with crystals everywhere at the two-month mark, and then unchanged after two years. “After a total of two years, this honestly did not change further,” he said. The test relied on storing the setup in a vacuum or a nitrogen-filled box between sessions to avoid oxidation.
The TIM in question is an alloy of gallium and indium, often including tin, which is liquid at room temperature (Thermal Grizzly sells its own as Conductonaut); gallium melts at about 30 degrees Celsius, with the gallium-indium-tin mix melting at only 11 degrees. During a recent InfoQ webinar titled "AI in Production: What Breaks, What Works, and Who Approves It?", a panel of senior engineering practitioners met to dissect the real-world operational challenges of deploying agentic systems. The discussion was moderated by Hien Luu and featured Zichuan Xiong and Prem Chandrasekaran from ThoughtWorks, privacy specialist Katharine Jarmul, and financial AI practitioner Lan Chu. Luu opened the session by noting three core drivers: AI fails differently from traditional software by generating convincing inaccuracies rather than crashing; coding agents are generating production code faster than humans can review; and sensitive data has new places to leak through prompts, context windows, and retrieved documents.
Xiong, Head of AI Ops for Managed Services at ThoughtWorks, highlighted the widespread issue of "semantic drift" in LLM pipelines. He described how text-to-SQL translation agents frequently flatten domain-specific concepts, such as treating "member" identically across sales and customer support domains, leading to subtle, hidden errors in downstream business analytics that pass standard tracing. Similarly, Chu recounted a critical failure caused by "embedding drift" in financial compliance systems. Nadie lo puso ahí para medir los glaciares y, sin embargo, medio siglo después, un equipo internacional ha rescatado sus imágenes para calcular a qué velocidad se mueve el hielo de Groenlandia y la Antártida.
Gracias a ello, sabemos que entre 1979 y 2023 hemos perdido 11,3 billones de toneladas de hielo polar.
Es, en fin, una cifra más. Una cifra enorme, descomunal, increíble; pero una cifra más. Por eso lo más interesante no es la cuenta, lo más interesante es cómo ha desaparecido todo ese hielo.
Cosas que hemos aprendido ahora. No es que esta metodología sea nueva, pero gracias al Landsat ahora tenemos una serie temporal mucho más larga. Eso, para empezar, nos ha permitido confirmar que el problema actual de pérdida de hielo polar tiene fecha.
En los años setenta y ochenta, los mantos estaban muy cerca del equilibrio. Para hacernos una idea, en términos generales Groenlandia perdía unas 60 gigatoneladas al año en los ochenta y casi lo mismo en los noventa. Con los 2000, la situación cambia y la cifra se triplicó (192). En la década de los 2010 las pérdidas llegaron a 264.
En la Antártida pasó algo parecido (y pasó de unas 48 gigatoneladas anuales a unas 202 en el mismo intervalo de tiempo.

articles.title: Tressfecta wants to make hair braiding a less arduous task for hairstylists | TechCrunch

Aisata Diallo, 24, calls herself a lifelong braider. “I’ve always braided my hair growing up and, at some point in my college career, started braiding other people’s hair,” she said. At Northeastern University in Boston, she found limited access to braiders and textured-hair specialists, so she decided to fill that gap by starting a small business of her own.
“Throughout that experience, I was very close to some of the pain points in the styling process and complained about it constantly,” she said. Braiding is a manual task, and a single style can take eight hours to complete. Many professionals deal with issues like cramping and carpal tunnel syndrome after spending long days standing behind a chair weaving hair into patterns.
At first, Diallo said she didn’t know what to do about it. “I stopped braiding, and one of the reasons that I stopped braiding was due to the physical toll it has on your body.” She wanted to find a way to make braiding less painful and wondered whether new AI technology could automate some part of the process. Building hardware for braiding is expensive, difficult, and complex, which is one reason there have been few innovations in this space. The textured hair market has also long been overlooked by the mainstream.

Epic introduces an improved version of anti-cheat for Linux — strict TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot rules spark open-source pushback, but finally allow Linux gamers to play Fortnite
Are all these requirements worth it just to play a few competitive titles?
Epic Games says that it’s working on an update for its anti-cheat solution for Linux that would close the gap in capabilities with the Windows version of Easy Anti-Cheat. The company said that EAC Linux V2 will use existing Linux features to make it easier for distribution maintainers to meet these requirements by default, which should allow more Linux gamers to play competitive titles without needing to make changes to their current setup, but with the trade-off of forced adherence to certain security measures that the Linux community often avoids.
EAC Linux V2 currently has the following requirements: Signed Kernel and Kernel Modules, TPM 2.0, Secure Boot, Measured Boot, Input-Output Memory Management Unit (IOMMU), Kernel Lockdown Integrity Mode, Kexec Disabled, and Linux Security Module BPF. The company says that it expects to iterate on these requirements over time, and that it’s looking to work with developers and distribution maintainers to refine these requirements. Using these features means that EAC Linux V2 will not need a kernel driver like the Windows implementation of anti-cheat, although it may require some distro maintainers to effect a configuration change to work with EAC Linux V2.

articles.title: Uber Automates Dependency Analysis Across Its Service Mesh
articles.summary:
Uber has developed an automated approach to mapping service dependencies and classifying how downstream failures propagate across its service mesh. The system uses RPC middleware to correlate caller and callee failures across production requests, classifying dependencies as fail-close, fail-open, or unknown. Uber says the approach has cataloged dependencies for critical APIs and indexed most fail-close anomalies across its service mesh.
The Uber Engineering team highlighted the motivation in a LinkedIn post,
When a request fails, how do you figure out what actually caused it? At Uber’s scale, that gets complicated fast. With thousands of services and dependencies interacting, traditional tracing can’t always give engineers the full picture quickly enough.
In a microservices architecture, requests can traverse deeply nested and asynchronous service calls, making it difficult to determine which dependency contributed to a failure. Uber defines a fail-close dependency as one whose failure can consistently cause its caller to fail. A fail-open dependency can fail without causing its caller to fail, while insufficient evidence results in an unknown classification. The classification can then be applied across call paths to identify how failures may propagate toward an originating API.
Uber initially considered distributed tracing for establishing these relationships, but found sampling too slow for rare failures. The company says more than 99.9% of requests complete without errors…

articles.title: Elorian’s first AI model wants to reason with images, not just about them | TechCrunch

Elorian, the Palo Alto AI startup that raised a $55 million seed round at a $300 million valuation before it launched a product, released its first model on Friday, TechCrunch has exclusively learned.
The model, Glimpse, is launching as a research preview with API access and a chat interface is waitlist-only, so for now it’s a results table and a thesis. The thesis? Today’s AI models, for all their skill with language and code, still can’t really see.
Most multimodal models look at an image once, convert it to tokens, and then reason about it in text — like describing a photo from memory. Glimpse keeps going back to the source. Mid-reasoning, it can crop into a region, pull specific frames from a video, or run code to measure or compare what it’s looking at, a mechanism Elorian calls a “visual scratch space.” Think of someone pinching to zoom on a phone photo to double-check what they thought they saw.
For former Google DeepMind researcher and Elorian CEO Andrew Dai, one of the clearest signs that AI still couldn’t really see came on game night.
Last year he photographed a board game he’d just finished with friends and asked a frontier model who was winning. It couldn’t say. Board games “each have their own visual language, each have their own iconography, symbols,” he told TechCrunch. “To an adult, it’s quite easy to understand what’s going on with minimal text, but these models aren’t able to intuit what the symbols mean.”

articles.title: Zod Brings In-Process Schema Compilation and a 9x Cut in Memory Footprint
articles.summary:
Zod, the TypeScript-first schema validation library created by Colin McDonnell, released Zod 4.5 on August 28, 2026, introducing schema compilation, an order-of-magnitude cut in schema memory usage, and a batch of long-requested helpers. Zod 4.6 followed on September 9, extending that work and fixing a recursive-schema memory regression. The major compilation and memory-footprint changes arrived in 4.5, which remains the focus here, but developers upgrading now should also account for the subsequent release.
The flagship addition is z.compile(), which turns any schema into a precompiled validator that parses the same data three to nine times faster. The compiled schema behaves exactly like the original, with no special rules. Importantly, as McDonnell explains, compilation happens in-process rather than at build time, so there is no bundler plugin or codegen step to wire up.
Teams that want this applied everywhere can add import "zod/compile" at the top of an entry point, or run node --import zod/compile app.js, after which every schema is compiled lazily the first time it parses data.
By memoising bound methods instead of allocating them per instance, a bare z.string() now retains 784 bytes of heap rather than 7.5kb, a roughly nine-fold reduction. safeParse() also skips stack-trace capture on failure, making invalid input about 7.5 times cheaper to reject. Marcher sur le sol lunaire provoque des échanges de charges entre les matériaux en contact. À cela s’ajoutent les interactions avec les particules chargées présentes dans l’environnement spatial.
La Lune ne bénéficie ni d’une atmosphère épaisse ni d’un champ magnétique global comme ceux de la Terre. Sa surface est donc largement exposée au vent solaire, ce flux de particules éjectées par notre étoile. Comme l’explique la NASA, les astronautes et les robots peuvent accumuler de l’électricité statique en se déplaçant sur son sol poussiéreux.
Mais le Soleil joue aussi un rôle utile : le vent solaire et les effets du rayonnement ultraviolet peuvent contribuer à évacuer les charges. Without this shift, organizations continue to rely on human judgment in high-risk workflows, leaving a critical gap that attackers are increasingly exploiting.

articles.title: Tesla turns to 50-year-old stunt technology as it tries to Roadster again

Nine years after first trying to resurrect the Roadster, Tesla is apparently trying again. CEO Elon Musk might have relocated its HQ to Texas, but yet again he has returned to California’s showbiz industry to hawk his wares; last time it was a Hollywood back lot for the remote-controlled Cybercab demo, last night it was decades-old stunt technology to make a show car do tricks in the air.
The new Roadster, we’re told, will be unlike anything else, although the angular, wedge-shaped styling owes more than a little to Giorgetto Giugiaro’s original Lotus Esprit—Musk is known to own a James Bond prop car—as well as the more recent Lamborghini Gallardo. At the rear are four giant exhaust pipes; these do not signal Tesla’s sudden embrace of hydrocarbons beyond those emitted by private aviation.

Prediction market boosters often tout the platforms as barometers of public opinion, or even “truth machines” offering a clearer picture of where things are headed than polling or other data. In 2024, for example, Kalshi beat many pollsters in forecasting the outcome of the US presidential race. But their trading activity can also tell more perplexing stories.
Two global election markets on Polymarket’s offshore platform, for instance, generated over $600 million in trading volume, far more than most political markets typically attract. Most of the activity took place buying and selling contracts tied to long-shot candidates who ultimately did not win.
This summer, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s Prosperity Party cruised to victory in federal elections, winning 438 parliamentary seats and paving the way for him to serve another five-year term. The closest competitor won 13 seats. On prediction markets, trading volume—the total value of contracts bought and sold—typically tracks roughly with the odds of a given outcome; frontrunners attract far more volume than long shots. But in this case, the trading patterns deviated sharply from the norm. Just $173,000 was wagered on Ahmed winning, compared to more than $41 million traded on his chief of staff, Shimelis Abdisa, becoming the country’s next leader. Altogether, the volume traded added up to over $285 million, nearly all on losing candidates.

This view runs counter to those who believe that robotics, powered by a general foundation model, is about to have its “ChatGPT moment” — that day when the shockingly capable chatbot was launched in late 2022. (General Intuition CEO Pim de Witte told Equity earlier this year that a single general foundation model would make much of today’s specialized robotics work redundant, and be that moment.)
On this episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Dominic-Madori Davis caught up with Vishwanath to discuss where she’s writing first checks as the founder and managing partner of Techable VC. They also talked about what she’s learned as one of the first women executives to spin out of Nvidia and launch her own early-stage firm investing in physical AI across robotics, materials science, and life sciences.

articles.title: Google EnvHarness Enables Self-Evolving Agents to Learn in Dynamics Environments
articles.summary:
Google researchers open sourced EnvHarness, a framework that dynamically adapts agent-training environments to an agent's weaknesses without modifying the agent, environment, or evaluation system. According to the researchers, this approach can improve both learning effectiveness and efficiency while helping agents overcome their weaknesses.
According to the research authors, self-evolving agents typically improve by rewriting their prompts and acquiring new skills, but rarely adapt the environments in which they operate. This has important consequences:
An agent that keeps improving against a frozen benchmark eventually stops learning from it. The start states, the rules and the feedback are the same for every learner at every stage, so once the agent can solve the tasks, the environment has nothing further to teach.
Environment generation, the researchers explain, is expensive, requiring domain-specific pipelines and often relying on expensive or unreliable verifiers Despite these efforts, the resulting environments remain static. To make it easier for engineers to train agent in adaptive environments, they created EnvHarness.
EnvHarness acts as a programmable layer of plug-in components that wraps a static environment, changing only the interface the agent interacts through. By dynamically introducing mutations, it can reshape the environment's behavior without altering its underlying structure or evaluation system.

articles.title: YouTube Music now labels AI-generated songs
articles.summary:
YouTube Music has added labels for songs that have been generated by AI.
Now, users will see a round icon that says AI right below the track name. YouTube says this label will be used on any content “where AI played a significant role.” This includes “using a generative model to create the composition and vocals,” notes YouTube. From there, you can tap the label to learn more information about how AI was used in the creation of the given song.
YouTube is the latest music streamer to introduce AI labels on its platform. In September, Spotify rolled out its own GenAI disclaimers, with Apple Music promising to do the same by the end of the year. Deezer also followed suit earlier this week. These moves come after major entertainment industry organizations like the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA), the Grammys, and SAG-AFTRA jointly called upon streamers to more clearly label AI music.
Overall, it’s always good to have more disclosure, especially where AI is concerned. In this day and age, more and more people want to be reassured that they’re supporting quality, ethically produced art instead of AI slop.

articles.title: India becomes the latest country to report rogue AI agent activity | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
AI agents from multiple providers accessed personal data and confidential material at Indian organizations during research and testing, India’s cybersecurity agency said Thursday.
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said it had received “multiple voluntary disclosures from AI model providers” whose models, during research and evaluation runs on the open internet, “had reached the live systems of Indian organizations.”
The agents got in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles, and their actions “exceeded the authorisation of their assigned tasks.”
This makes India the latest stop on what has become a world tour for rogue AI agents. In July, OpenAI’s agents escaped a test environment and hacked French company Hugging Face — kicking off a summer of rogue AI agent activity. Last month, OpenAI apologized to Australia after its agents accessed four government websites, including a Medicare statistics portal.
At Hugging Face, OpenAI’s agents started the same way but then found and exploited software flaws to run code on the company’s servers. CERT-In described no such hacking in India, where the agents appear to have simply used the access left lying around.

Face à la pression des constructeurs qui craignaient des amendes record et à la concurrence agressive de la Chine, les deux pays ont dû faire des compromis pour le « Made in Europe ». Voici ce qui va concrètement changer pour l’industrie automobile européenne.
Le 100 % électrique en 2035 a du plomb dans l’aile, vive les « supercrédits »
L’Union européenne avait fixé à 100 % la réduction des émissions de CO₂ à l’échappement des voitures neuves en 2035. C’est fini. Si le texte officiel affiche toujours l’objectif d’une baisse de 90 % des émissions de CO2 (sans mécanisme de compensation), une astuce comptable vient tout changer : les « supercrédits ».
Pour faire simple, la vente d’une petite voiture électrique fabriquée en Europe comptera désormais pour 1,4 vente dans les calculs de réduction d’émissions des constructeurs. Un modèle électrique standard vaudra, lui, 1,2 vente. Finalement, selon les calculs de l’Institut Mobilités en Transition, les industriels n’auront en réalité besoin de vendre qu’environ 72 % de voitures électriques (dopées par ces supercrédits) en moyenne pour atteindre les objectifs.

Damit vollziehen die Wissenschaftler:innen konzeptionell eine Abkehr von der zentralisierten Energieversorgung hin zu einem dezentralen Modell. „Unser Körper ist ein Kraftwerk, das rund um die Uhr in Betrieb ist“, erklärt Hauptautorin Siqi Wang in einer Mitteilung der Universität. Maybe it was the grey color, the slightly bulbous roofline, or the vaguely SUV-like proportions of the electric Porsche Macan, but as I shuttled kids and groceries around city and suburban streets, I never once noticed a longing stare from other drivers. Unlike with other cars I’ve tested, no enthusiasts stopped to ask me questions.
The 2026 Porsche Macan Turbo simply blended in, leaving in its wake a raft of existential questions. What is a sports car, anyway? Does it need to be overwhelmingly extroverted? Should it match the leaner, lighter look of its gas-powered sibling?
Drive one and the questions cease. Maybe that’s because the acceleration makes it hard to breathe? Or maybe it’s because, by the numbers, the Macan is a sports car at heart despite its rather humdrum crossover body style.
My passengers would agree. The kids I drove to soccer practice, both my own and others, gave the punchy acceleration high marks. The G-forces it reports on the head-up display ($2,660) can easily mimic the pull of gravity. Stab the accelerator at 70 mph and it lurches as though it were standing still. (Don’t worry, fellow parents. I did not try that with children on board.)
On winding roads, the car comes alive, thanks in part to the four-wheel steering ($2,150). Drop it into Sport Plus mode, and the car literally drops on its air suspension. Are we sure this is another anonymous crossover? Maybe anonymity is a useful trait in a car this responsive and powerful.

In 2023, FDA scientists determined that the peptides lacked data on safety and efficacy and posed risks. articles.title: En la década de 1950, Argentina liberó faisanes asiáticos en una isla de la Patagonia: hoy dominan sus bosques y preocupan a los científicos
articles.summary:
Durante la primera miad del siglo XX, estancieros, cazadores y funcionarios de la administración de Parques Nacionales de Argentina se propusieron convertir la isla Victoria, a pocos kilómetros en barco de Bariloche, en una rarísima 'arca de Noé'.
De una forma u otra se introdujeron ciervos europeos, jabalíes y todo tipo de árboles exóticos; no solo plantaron secuoyas californianas, extraviaron gatos (asilvestrados) o importaron visones americanos: es que, en la década de los 50, soltaron toda clase de pavos reales, gallinas de Guinea y hasta cinco tipos de faisán.
La idea era "aprovechar" la problemática gestión privada anterior y convertir la isla en un punto turístico de gran interés por su fauna (nativa o exótica) y fomentar la caza en la región. Pero aquello descarriló pronto y para 1959, la estación estaba cerrada, abandona y dejada de la mano de Dios.
Setenta años después, de esas siete especies de aves, solo queda una.
Los inmortales, versión patagónica. Entre junio de 2011 y mayo de 2012, un equipo del CONICET y la Universidad Autónoma del Comahue colocó ocho cáaras trampa en la isla. Gracias a ello acumularon 710 registros independientes de mamíferos y aves terrestres.
Es curioso (o no tanto), pero solo dos se correspondían con especies nativas: el chucao y el ratón colilargo. El resto eran gamos, ciervos, jabalíes, visones y faisanes. 222 de esos registros eran faisanes.

articles.title: Holzalkohol im Weltraum entdeckt: Was das für Planetenforschung bedeutet
articles.summary:
1.000 Lichtjahre entfernt: Wissenschaftler:innen entdecken Holzalkohol im Weltraum
Holzalkohol ist in der Industrie von großer Bedeutung. Die klare, farblose und leicht flüchtige Flüssigkeit ist ein wichtiger Grundstoff zur Herstellung von Kunststoffen, Formaldehyd, Essigsäure und Farben. Außerdem ist er auch ein Bestandteil von Frostschutzmitteln.
Holzalkohol spielt als organisches Molekül auch eine wesentliche Rolle bei der Bildung komplexer organischer Moleküle im Weltraum. Im Rahmen des „ALMA COMPASS“-Forschungsprogramms wurde nun vollständig deuteriertes Methanol, sogenanntes „schweres Methanol“ (CD3OD), in der Umgebung des Protosterns IRAS4A2 nachgewiesen. Forscher:innen des Max Planck Instituts in Garching sind besonders neugierig, da sie sich die dort beobachtete Menge nicht erklären können.
These: Moleküle reagieren bereits vor der Stern-Entstehung
Wissenschaftler:innen haben bereits Hinweise auf weitere komplexe Moleküle, etwa Isopropanol, das als Reinigungsalkohol bekannt ist, in der Umgebung sehr junger Sternsysteme gefunden. Experimente deuten darauf hin, dass diese Moleküle wahrscheinlich auf der Oberfläche eisiger Staubkörner in kalten Nebelwolken entstehen.
Dort reagieren sie langsam mit Kohlenstoff, Sauerstoff, Wasserstoff und anderen Atomen zu immer komplexeren Verbindungen – und das lange, bevor ein neuer Stern überhaupt entsteht. articles.title: “thegentlemanpervert” producing AI CSAM is a NJ prosecutor, say cops
articles.summary:
New Jersey’s deputy attorney general, Brian Richard Fitzgerald, was arrested on “felony charges related to AI-generated child sexual abuse material (CSAM),” Bucks County Detectives said in a press release Thursday.
In the US, cops have vowed to crack down on AI CSAM since at least 2024, when the Department of Justice made one of the earliest arrests. After charging a Wisconsin man with spreading “thousands of realistic images of prepubescent minors” across Telegram and Instagram, the DOJ clarified to law enforcement that “CSAM generated by AI is still CSAM.”
On Thursday, New Jersey officials accused 51-year-old Fitzgerald of using AI to make photos from social media of real minors into sexualized images that he then distributed on social media.
Fitzgerald was charged after the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children received a tip that a Discord user shared an illicit image in July. Cops then used “digital forensics and subscriber records” linked to the Discord account and “associated Internet protocol addresses” to track the user to Fitzgerald’s home address.
After a search Thursday, cops “recovered prompts and scripts used to create artificially generated child sexual abuse material using an AI program,” the press release said. They also found Discord chat logs where Fitzgerald, under the Discord username “thegentlemanpervert_2160_07833,” allegedly “admitted to making multiple illicit images using artificial intelligence and sharing them with other users.”

articles.title: Descubren que las enanas blancas no son blancas. Al menos no todas
articles.summary:
Desde pequeños, siempre que hemos pintado estrellas las hemos coloreado de amarillo. Como mucho, de mayores sabemos que también pueden ser rojas, azules o blancas. Esa es, más o menos, su escala de colores. Hay estrellas que incluso dan pistas sobre su color, como la gigante roja o la enana blanca. Sin embargo, según un nuevo estudio, la gama de colores puede ser mucho más amplia, especialmente en el caso de las enanas blancas.
Rosas, verdes y púrpuras. Las enanas blancas están demasiado lejos para que podamos verlas directamente y mucho menos interpretar su color. Por eso, un equipo de científicos de la Universidad de Warwick ha usado espectros tomados previamente y los han pasado por un modelo informático que analiza la luz como si estuviese pasando por los fotorreceptores del ojo humano. Así, vieron que, si bien es cierto que la mayoría de enanas blancas se verían blancas si las tuviéramos delante, algunas se mostrarían ante nuestros ojos con un bonito color verde, rosa o púrpura. Y también habría azules o amarillas.
La evolución esperada de una estrella. Generalmente, el color de las estrellas se asocia con su temperatura, exactamente igual que pasa con un hierro que se va calentando cada vez más. Los fotones azules son mucho más energéticos que los amarillos o rojos. Por eso, a medida que se calienta la estrella, va pasando primero por tonos más cálidos y finalmente por colores fríos, llegando primero al blanco y finalmente al azul.
