articles.title: La Ley de Propiedad Horizontal lo permite y los expertos lo confirman: "Puedes instalar una barandilla en tu plaza para que no rayen tu coche"
articles.summary:
Hay decisiones que nos parecen de lo más lógico y racional que a ojos de otras personas pueden parecer surrealistas. Y todo lo contrario. En ese sentido, no hay ningún lugar en este mundo para ver las dos caras de una misma moneda que una junta de vecinos. Quizás ahí reside el éxito de cuentas en redes sociales como Líos de vecinos.
Una de sus particulares historias ha vuelto a alcanzar la viralidad.
Sólo le rayé el coche. Esta cuenta de Instagram trae en uno de sus post la de historia de dos conductores. Uno dice haber rayado sin querer el coche del vecino de al lado, dejando una nota para abrir un parte amistoso y que los seguros se pusieran en contacto.
La decisión de su vecino, sin embargo, fue radical: denunciarle a la policía e instalar una barandilla para evitar que ambos coches volvieran a tocarse. Ahora, el primero de ellos, dice no poder abrir la puerta del coche.
No hace falta explicar por qué el post se ha hecho viral.
¿Qué dice la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal? La normativa general a aplicar en estos casos dice que, efectivamente, el propietario puede hacer las modificaciones en su parcela que quiera. Siempre y cuando no produzca un problema a otros vecinos. Así, en el artículo 7.1 de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal se lee lo siguiente:
El propietario de cada piso o local podrá modificar los elementos arquitectónicos, instalaciones o servicios de aquél cuando no menoscabe o altere la seguridad del edificio, su estructura general, su configuración o estado exteriores…

Un modèle entraîné sur des collisions de particules

Presque chaque jour sur Mars, c’est un nuage de 1 600 kilomètres qui se forme puis disparaît en quelques heures. Un phénomène qui a lieu près d’Arsia Mons, un volcan situé près de l’équateur de la planète rouge. Sa formation pourrait passer par un processus physique connu en théorie, mais jamais observé directement dans l’atmosphère d’une planète, comme l’explique une étude publiée dans Nature Geoscience.
Ce nuage qui se forme sur Mars est appelé Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC) avec une longueur qui peut atteindre 1 800 kilomètres et une largeur d’environ 150 kilomètres. Son apparition a lieu au lever du jour avant de s’étirer vers l’ouest à plus de 600 kilomètres par heure puis de disparaître vers midi.
Un nuage sur Mars formé sans poussière
C’est pendant 80 jours lors du printemps et de l’été de l’hémisphère sud de Mars qu’a lieu sa période d’activité avec une composition faite de glace d’eau qui ne vient pas d’une éruption du volcan. Mais le volcan Arsia Mons explique pourquoi ce nuage est toujours au même endroit.
Le volcan Arsia Mons atteint environ 20 kilomètres de haut, soit plus de deux fois la hauteur de l’Everest. Les vents font alors monter de l’air humide de plusieurs kilomètres en quelques minutes. Hundreds of thousands of spam emails are carrying .ics attachments
- Phishing campaigns are abusing calendar invites and meeting requests to steal Microsoft 365 credentials
- Attackers hide malicious links in .ics files, fake meeting details, QR codes, and invite pages
- Researchers observed hundreds of thousands of phishing emails targeting over 40,000 organizations
If you get a calendar invite in your inbox be wary - it might be a carefully created phishing lure, designed to have you hand over Microsoft 365 or other login credentials.
Security firm Check Point Research (CPR) recently sounded the alarm for “several large-scale phishing campaigns,” abusing the fact that businesspeople routinely share calendar invites, and all designed to harvest their victim’s credentials.
Different approach, same result
CPR says it identified two separate approaches. In some cases, the threat actors would share calendar invites as .ics attachments. These pass email filters (since the file type itself is harmless) and land directly into people’s inboxes. In other cases, the invites would come as links (which end up redirecting the victim away from their calendar and right into a trap).
The former is arguably more dangerous: the attachment is disguised as a meeting request or a payment notification, and when the recipient opens or accepts the invitation, it ends up in their calendar. Sometimes, dependin…

articles.title: Critical PwnEscape Linux Kernel Vulnerability Lets Guest VMs Read Host Memory
articles.summary:
A newly disclosed critical flaw in the Linux kernel allows code inside a virtual machine to read memory on the host computer it runs on. A researcher demonstrated the leak against Vercel's live cloud sandboxes, and Vercel confirmed it.
The flaw, now tracked as CVE-2026-99999 and nicknamed PwnEscape, is in the Linux kernel's networking code, not in any one cloud's setup, so it reaches the shared layer that cloud providers use to keep customers' workloads apart.
It was found in a Vercel security challenge and reported privately before any public release, and there is no sign it has been used in a real attack.
What the Researcher Showed
Paulos Yibelo of the security firm pwn.ai found that specially made network packets sent from inside a virtual machine could do three things, he explained in a technical write-up: read the host's memory, crash the host, and run code on it. All three come from the same kernel flaw.
Vercel said in its report on the challenge that the memory leak was demonstrated against its production sandboxes. Each packet the guest sent out could carry back about 32 bytes of the host's memory, and the guest could keep going as long as it kept sending packets.
The crash and code execution were observed only on the researcher's own machines, which were set up to match Vercel's. Two specially crafted packets were enough to crash a host and take down every sandbox running on it.

A recent proxyjacking campaign spotted by security researchers GreyNoise impacted hundreds of devices in dozens of countries.
Proxyjacking
Proxyjacking is a type of attack in which a device is hijacked and assimilated into a proxy network. Usually, cybercriminals would break into a computer, install malware and create a proxy network of their own, which they can later rent or use themselves. Threat actors are always in need of “clean” and unflagged devices and IP addresses behind which they can hide, making residential proxies - both malicious and legal - highly wanted services.

articles.title: PEERSTITCH Malware Deployed via FortiOS Flaw Bypasses Checks on Tagged VPN Sessions

A suspected advanced threat actor has been observed exploiting a security flaw in Fortinet FortiOS to deliver a previously unreported memory-resident ARM64 malware known as PEERSTITCH.
The attack involves the exploitation of CVE-2025-61624 (CVSS score: 5.4), a path traversal flaw in the command line interpreter of FortiOS, FortiPAM, FortiProxy, and FortiSwitchManager that could allow a privileged attacker to achieve arbitrary write or delete files via specifically crafted arguments to existing commands. It was patched by Fortinet in April 2026.
"PEERSTITCH leaves no persistent binary on disk, opens no listening ports and initiates no outbound network connections," Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 researchers Daniel Gott and Shawn Westfall said. "Instead, it communicates through traffic generated by legitimate processes on the infected host, which makes the malware resistant to conventional endpoint and network detection."
The cybersecurity company said it discovered the activity as part of its prolonged network intrusion against a telecommunications managed service provider that took place in September 2024. The multi-stage network intrusion is being tracked as CL-STA-0954 (aka UNC5820), with initial access obtained by exploiting a critical Fortinet FortiManager flaw dubbed FortiJump (CVE-2024-47575).

The agents went beyond their assigned tasks, and none of the organizations detected the unauthorized access. After internal reviews, the AI companies whose models were being tested voluntarily reported the cases to CERT-In, India's national cyber agency.
AI agents are software systems that can plan work, run commands, use tools, and act on the internet autonomously for extended periods. In these cases, the agents gained access via credentials and connection settings left exposed in application configuration and public code repositories, and via cloud service roles with excessive permissions.
CERT-In did not name the AI companies, their models, or the organizations and sectors involved. It did not say how many companies reported cases or how many organizations were affected, and said only that the reports came in recently.

A local privilege escalation exploit published today gains root on OpenBSD 7.9 by chaining a roughly 37-year-old integer overflow with a separate kernel flaw, bypassing OpenBSD's KARL kernel-address randomization and its SMAP and SMEP hardware protections. Security firm Calif, which found and reported the flaws, published a detailed writeup and full proof-of-concept code after OpenBSD shipped patches for both issues in September.
The integer overflow in the shmat(4) attach function was fixed in errata 018, shipped September 14 as a reliability fix. The reference-counting use-after-free that completes the chain was fixed separately in errata 026, shipped September 30 as a security fix.
Both are available through syspatch and cover all architectures. OpenBSD 7.8 also received the integer-overflow fix.
The integer overflow, the entry point for the full chain, is classified as a reliability fix, not a security fix.
No CVE has been assigned for either flaw as of publication. There is no evidence that the vulnerabilities have been used in attacks.
The shared-memory attachment counter shm_nattch is defined as a signed 16-bit short with a maximum value of 32,767 in original BSD sources dating to 1988. OpenBSD inherited the type and never widened it.

If you're a fan of OLED, there's an exciting new acronym you need to know: FLiPP. It stands for FMM-Less innovative Pixel Patterning, and the FMM bit refers to fine metal masks. Those are normally used in OLED manufacturing to precisely place the organic emissive materials.
With FLiPP, there's no mask. Instead, the materials are deposited across the glass, given a protective layer and then refined using photolithography and etching to get rid of the unwanted sections.
The biggest single advantage to FLiPP is efficiency. According to trade site The Elec, LG Display found that the tech increased the utilization rate – the efficiency of the production – from 75% in a conventional FMM process to over 93% in a FLiPP process.
That's good news for us, because more efficient production means lower production costs. And that ultimately means we could see much better OLEDs without higher prices.

articles.title: Crean un modelo de IA que promete detectar el rechazo cardíaco tras un trasplante: cómo funciona
articles.summary:
Solo en 2024 se realizaron más de 10.000 trasplantes de corazón en 59 países, según el Observatorio Global de Donación y Trasplante. Se trata de una intervención que puede salvar la vida del paciente, pero que exige una vigilancia constante. El principal riesgo tras la cirugía es el rechazo del órgano, es decir, que el sistema inmunitario del receptor identifique al corazón donado como un cuerpo extraño y lo ataque.
Para detectar ese rechazo a tiempo, la medicina ha dependido durante décadas de la biopsia endomiocárdica, un procedimiento que consiste en extraer quirúrgicamente un pequeño fragmento del músculo cardíaco y analizarlo bajo el microscopio en busca de inflamación u otros signos de alerta.
En los últimos años, dos análisis de sangre conocidos como AlloMap y AlloSure se sumaron al arsenal diagnóstico. El primero mide la actividad de ciertos genes vinculados al rechazo celular; el segundo rastrea fragmentos de ADN del donante en el torrente sanguíneo del receptor. Ambos resultan eficaces para descartar el rechazo cuando los resultados son negativos, pero comparten una debilidad: generan con frecuencia falsos positivos, lo que deriva en biopsias que, en definitiva, resultan innecesarias.
Un equipo de investigadores de NYU Langone Health desarrolló un modelo de inteligencia artificial que combina esos biomarcadores sanguíneos con electrocardiogramas, los registros de la actividad eléctrica del corazón que se obtienen mediante sensores colocados sobre la piel.
